analyst_view.overall: Early view: Lugano top the league phase with nine points and 11 goals, having beaten Red Star 3-2, won 5-2 at Getafe and beaten Kauno Zalgiris 3-0; they also led the Swiss league in the latest table I could read. Jablonec (23rd, two points) under Lubos Kozel are hard to beat at home, holding Brighton to 0-0 in October, and drew 1-1 at Riga last time. The site's numbers rate this as close to even; on form I would favour Lugano.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little higher: Lugano's three games have produced 5, 7 and 3 goals, and Jablonec's earlier trip to Freiburg ended 3-2. Jablonec's 0-0 with a rotated Brighton side is the warning that they can shut games down at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec. Jablonec were dangerous from corners against Brighton (Rusek headed one narrowly wide), but Lugano should have plenty of the ball. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. No referee is known yet and neither side has a disciplinary pattern in this competition that I could find, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.7 shots. Lugano attack in numbers, and Jablonec will also go for it at home; the high number already captures that, so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Lugano's 11 goals in three games show sharp finishing, while Jablonec's keeper Jan Hanus kept Brighton out with several saves. I see nothing to move the number.
